scenes.headline: Orcas make waves on purpose.
scenes.body: Some pods in Antarctica hunt seals by knocking them off ice floes.

scenes.headline: They swim in a line, then dive together.
scenes.body: The coordinated rush creates a single wave big enough to wash the seal into the water.

scenes.headline: It's learned, not instinct.
scenes.body: Only certain pods do it, and calves practise for years before they get it right.

scenes.headline: One sourced wildlife fact, every day.
scenes.body: Save this one for a friend who loves the ocean.

caption:
Orcas in the Antarctic Peninsula have a hunting technique that looks like teamwork from a movie: they line up, charge an ice floe and dive at the last second, creating a wave that washes seals off the ice.

It's culture, not instinct — only some pods do it, and young orcas take years to learn.

Source: Pitman & Durban (2012), Marine Mammal Science. Photos: Callan Carpenter via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0 / CC BY 4.0.
